standing_assumptions: Section 1.1, pp.2–3: a countably infinite universe U and countably infinite collection L have fixed known bijective enumerations. The U order induces the rank order on each language K.

grouped_components: Existence of an eventually consistent optimal upper-density generator at identity deadlines.

GCG keeps a candidate list G of guesses that are strict supersets of the immediately preceding guess, stage m initially 0, and thresholds alpha_m=1/2-2^-m. Stage 0 outputs from current Accurate guess; later stages output earliest on-time unused elements of g_m. When a next candidate exists and current density reaches alpha_m, advance stage.

Proof has three cases: G always empty; G unbounded, with K claimed to recur in G and each stage terminating; G finite nonempty, whose last candidate is claimed to be K. Greedy production in a fixed stage gives mu_i≥floor((i-2T)/2)/i, and thresholds approach one half.

Section 4 remarks that identity deadlines suffice for optimal upper density and quantitatively separate timely upper and lower density. Global half-density optimality is contextualized by the turn-taking bound on p.3 and in Appendix E.

The interfaces support semantic and, for the named totalized generator, online guarantees; neither side supplies ordinary finite runtime bounds.

source_issues_preserved: The Algorithm 2 stage-advance test is printed even at m=0, where g_0 has not been defined. The accompanying prose says transition to m=1 once G is nonempty; this convention is not explicitly guarded in the pseudocode.
The displayed empirical-density expression uses a numeric third argument t or i, although the original mu_i definition takes a deadline function. The proof expands it as the identity deadline.

Accurate is imported with only eventual-subset and infinitely-often-correct properties stated locally. The finite-list arguments reason from a later correct guess to a strict-superset transition from its immediate predecessor; no additional nesting or transition property is explicitly supplied.

The proof concludes the upper-density lower bound in all three cases and ends with wording referring to a first claim; it does not separately present a final eventual-consistency argument, although Theorem 12 asserts it.
Ordinary computation of strict language inclusion and OnTimeUnused is not specified; the deterministic guarantee is in the abstract language-access model.
limitations: Statement and definition correspondence only: no theorem proof bodies, raw Lean comments, compilation, effective-computability certification, or human review certification.
All absence conclusions are limited to the supplied frozen interface/census, not unseen repository modules.
Frozen source ambiguity notes are retained separately from translation findings; no developer explanations were opened.
assessment: A fixed deterministic online semantic generator has eventual consistency and universal upper-density ≥1/2, plus a named adversarial presentation attaining equality, for the formal metric. This substantially covers the existential upper-density phenomenon. It is not literal Algorithm 2/Theorem 12: the guaranteed witness uses every accurate-guess time via its stage, not the printed strict-rise candidate list; the identity-deadline boundary also differs under direct index transport.

algorithm_scope: Scoped definitions and statement guarantees inspected: Accurate selector, totalized state/history/output, online-prefix invariance, native strict-rise machine, and adaptive equality witness. No theorem proof correctness, equivalence of the two machines or effective finite computation is certified.
strength: The universal lower bound uses a stricter direct-transport deadline and independent per-language orders, so it is stronger in these aspects. Equality is witnessed for every target, stronger than merely one global infimum witness, within that formal metric. Literal named-algorithm identity is lost; exact equality for the looser source metric is not a consequence of strict-metric equality alone. Thus no single overall stronger/weaker ordering or exact correspondence is asserted.

discrepancies.detail: Named guaranteed totalized witness differs materially from source Algorithm 2. It could serve as an alternate existential witness, but justification as a repair awaits Stage 3.

OnTimeUnusedRank is t<r; source identity allows output at its rank deadline. Under the direct 1-to-0 index map the source identity is r+1. This is a substantive credit-boundary difference, not automatically a vanishing initial error.
Equal-language order coherence is required, but a single common universe preference order across unequal languages is not. Restricting to source-compatible orders is possible semantically.
The exact-density presentation and main consistency/lower bound already coexist on the same named output; no source theorem is missing solely because another endpoint has conditional exceptions.
Prefix causality/online equality are supplied natively, but full-language inclusion and real decisions remain classical and have no runtime guarantee.
